Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
205 PM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 204 PM EST Friday...

Increased pops and precipitation amounts Saturday into Sunday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 204 PM EST Friday...

1. A cooler and unsettled weather pattern is expected this 
weekend with some summit level wet snow possible on Sunday morning.  

2. Continued unsettled flow with temperatures falling towards 
the end of next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 204 PM EST Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The forecast challenge this weekend is evolution of 
closed mid/upper lvl cyclonic circulation and track of sfc low pres 
and associated pops and qpf placement. Sfc analysis shows stationary 
boundary draped along the Eastern Seaboard with axis of showers and 
embedded thunderstorms. Meanwhile, GOES-19 water vapor imagery shows 
a potent/compact closed cyclonic circulation over the central Great 
Lakes this aftn with north side deformation/moisture over the 
northern Lakes. This circulation is progged to move southeast toward 
the Southern Tier of NY by 00z Sunday, while north side deformation 
and mid lvl moisture axis lifting from southwest to northeast acrs 
our cwa on Sat aftn. The mid/upper lvl circulation tries to capture 
sfc low pres by late Sat into Sunday with weak inverted sfc trof 
developing acrs our cwa. The combination of weak sfc convergence and 
mid lvl deformation on north/northwest side of closed 850-700mb 
cyclonic circulation supports high categorical (85-100%) Sat aft 
into Sunday acrs most of our cwa. As 1000mb sfc low pres lifts acrs 
eastern Maine on Sunday brisk/northwest upslope flow develops under 
modest low level caa. It should be noted the airmass behind this 
system is only marginally cool enough to support summit lvls snow, 
given progged 850mb temps near 0C and 925mb of 1C to 3C. Any snow 
accumulations wl be above 3000 ft and generally a dusting to 1 inch, 
maybe 1 to 3 inches above 4000 ft acrs the High Peaks in Essex 
County, NY. Rainfall amounts will be 0.30" to 0.60" with localized 
higher amounts possible in favorable upslope areas of the northern 
Dacks and central/northern Greens. This general idea of higher pops 
and qpf is supported by the latest AI-GFS/AI-ECWMF 12z/06z runs
respectively. Much cooler temps wl be expected this weekend, 
especially on Sunday with brisk northwest winds/damp conditions 
and highs only in the 40s. 

Next potent s/w energy in the progressive northwest flow aloft 
arrives on Monday with additional widespread precip likely, 
especially favorable upslope areas. Progged thickness values are 
cooler for this system, along with progged 850mb temps btwn -1C 
and - 3C, supporting slightly lower snow levels. However, still
some uncertainty on amount of moisture in nw flow aloft with pw
values in the 0.30 and 0.40 range and limited pocket of mid lvl
moisture. For now have kept close to NBM pops/qpf and thermal 
profiles, but expect changes to occur as it becomes a near term 
forecast focus. Highs Monday wl range from the mid 30s to upper 
40s acrs our region.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The large scale cyclonic gyre over the Hudson Bay will 
continue to eject several shortwaves through mid to late next week. 
Tuesday and Wednesday will see shower chances focused in the higher 
terrain, with perhaps some blocking against the Greens pushing 
moisture into the Champlain Valley either day. The most robust of 
the two days looks to be Tuesday, with a more defined vort max 
tracking near the International Border. Thermal profiles Tuesday 
into Wednesday would be supportive of some nighttime snow potential 
in the higher terrain upslope favored regions above 2500ft, with 
light accumulations possible given the prolonged period of 925-850mb 
temperatures at or below 0 through mid week. Below 2500ft, mainly 
rain is to be expected, with little in the way of impacts. Should 
Mount Mansfield still be holding onto the latest 1" snowfall, of 
which the record is November 9th, it appears currently that we will 
have a high chance to reach 1" at the latest by Wednesday morning. 
By the late week, ensembles are coming into better agreement that a 
mid/upper level closed low will develop and swing through the area. 
This would point towards sharply cooler daytime highs as 850mb 
temperatures will fall to near -5C, supporting highs in the upper 
30s to low 40s across the area Thursday, and especially Friday, with 
some chances for some light shower activity.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 18Z Saturday...The area remains lodged between a coastal
system to our east, and an upper low to our west, with dry and
generally clear VFR conditions in between. The next 6 hours should
remain VFR with increasing clouds from the west. Additionally, some
light rain may be possible at MSS, but probabilities under 40%, and
no impacts expected. Beyond 00Z, ceilings will lower towards MVFR
the west and the east, converging in the Champlain Valley. This
convergence signature is leading to increased confidence in a period
of IFR for most terminals, outside of PBG, overnight tonight. Have
begun to denote IFR cigs for BTV/SLK/EFK/RUT/MPV beginning between
05-07Z, with the expectation that IFR chances will remain at least
through 10-11Z for BTV/EFK , with perhaps a bit longer at RUT/MPV
due to increasing moisture associated with the coastal system. IFR
ceilings probabilities are around 40-50% for the aforementioned
terminals. Visibilities will likely see some MVFR to high IFR
reductions as well with periods of drizzle and light showers in
association with the lowering cigs. MSS will be the most complex
terminal tonight and tomorrow as the upper low passes directly
overhead with variable ceilings between high IFR and low MVFR,
though predictability remains low. Showers and some drizzle, with
associated cigs 800- 1800ft agl will continue towards the end of the
TAF period, with generally light and variable winds. Some northerly
channeled flow to 10 knots is expected by tomorrow afternoon at
BTV/PBG/MSS.

Outlook...

Saturday Night: Mainly IFR, with local MVFR possible. Definite
RA.
Sunday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely RA, Chance
SHRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA, Slight chance SHSN.
Veterans Day: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

VT...None.
NY...None.
